newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end up as ITC leads surprise rally.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end up as ITC leads surprise rally.

text.p: Bombay shares sprung higher in late trade on Monday on the back of a nearly ten percent jump in index-linked stock ITC, traders said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark index ended 51.53 points, or 1.37 percent, higher at a provisional 3806.63.
Traders said ITC shares leapt 42 rupees, or nearly ten percent, to end at 478.50.
"The market is very short on ITC. Some speculators have realised that and are squeezing the shorts," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Traders said some speculators had to cover their short positions after leading foreign funds turned buyers in the stock last week. They said the fund buying continued in this session.
"It was a double whammy -- foreign institutional buying and short covering in expectation of an auction on the National Stock Exchange this week," one dealer said.
ITC shares attracted a backwardation charge -- indicating a short position -- in the BSE carry forward account ended May 31.
"It was the third consecutive backwardation," the trader at the foreign brokerage said. "Along with ITC, everything is following suit."
ITC shares gained 30.75 rupees to 475.25 on the National Stock Exchange.
Funds were also buyers in leading soaps and detergents maker Hindustan Lever, tea firm Tata Tea and scooter and motorcycle maker Bajaj Auto.
Traders said the market was looking towards an impending hike in the prices of some petroleum products.
Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Saturday said the decision-making Steering Committee of the United Front will meet on June 8 to reach a consensus on increasing oil prices.
"There are four or five options to tackle the oil pool deficit," Gujral told reporters before leaving for New Delhi after a day-long visit to Bombay.
He said the committee will consider these options and would have to arrive at a consensus decision at their June 8 meeting.
"We have had a lot of talk so far, but the government has shown a lot of incompetence in taking decisions," said a local trader.
